(countable, uncountable) Power, strength, force, or influence held by a person or group.
(uncountable) Physical strength or force.
s.x: He pushed with all his might, but still it would not move.

s.g: (uncountable) The ability to do something.
(obsolete) Mighty; powerful.
(obsolete) Possible.
Used to indicate a desired past action that was not done.
s.x: You might have warned me about the thunderstorm.

s.g: (auxiliary) Used to indicate conditional or possible actions; would perhaps/maybe.
s.x: Well, I might go to the party on Sunday, but I haven't decided yet.

s.g: (auxiliary) Used concessively to admit something before making a more accurate or important statement; although
s.x: I might be in a wheelchair, but I still want to be treated as a lady.

s.g: (auxiliary, UK, meiosis) Used to express certainty.
s.x: Yeah, I think we might need something a bit sturdier.

s.g: (auxiliary, often archaic) Used in polite requests for permission.
s.x: "Might I take the last biscuit? I wonder if I might have a little more coffee too." "Yes you may, help yourself.".

s.g: used to express the possibility of something occurring in the past as condition to another non-occurring past event
s.x: If we had gone to Hollywood, we might've met a film star.

s.g: used to express uncertainty about a past event
s.x: I think I might've left my umbrella on the train.

Traveller or worker who moves from one region or country to another.

Any of various pierid butterflies of the genus Catopsilia. Also called an emigrant.
Migratory.
(intransitive) To relocate periodically from one region to another, usually according to the seasons.
s.x: Twice a year the geese migrate — from Florida to Canada and back again.

s.g: (intransitive) To change one's geographic pattern of habitation.
s.x: Many groups had migrated to western Europe from the plains of eastern Europe.

s.g: (intransitive) To change habitations across a border; to move from one country or political region to another.
s.x: To escape persecution, they migrated to a neutral country.

s.g: (intransitive) To move slowly towards, usually in groups.
s.x: Once the hosts started bickering in the kitchens, the guests began to migrate towards the living room.

s.g: (intransitive) To move gradually, especially from an intended to an unintended position.
s.x: Oil was able to migrate from the accessory gearbox into the magneto housing through the improperly installed gland seals.

s.g: An instance of moving to live in another place for a while.

Movement in general.
s.x: The migration of lead from a can to the food inside it can cause lead poisoning.
